prompt.context: Our client is the Dean of Kellogg School of Management. She has hired you to advise her on an idea which struck her during the previous week: to consider starting a satellite campus of Kellogg in India.
prompt.question: Should Kellogg enter the Indian market by opening a satellite campus? Please determine whether this is a sound strategic and financial move.

clarifying_info.q: What is the strategic rationale behind starting a campus in India?
clarifying_info.a: India is one of the fastest-growing economies with huge demand for business education both domestically and from students travelling abroad. Dean Sally believes it would help Kellogg move to the Top 3. She wants the satellite campus to break even in 4 years.

clarifying_info.q: Will there be any compromise on student quality or admissions standards?
clarifying_info.a: No. The quality of students and the selection procedure would be comparable to the current Kellogg procedure. There will be no compromise on the quality of applicants to increase revenue.

clarifying_info.q: Who is the local competition in India?
clarifying_info.a: India has its own top-tier business schools including the 7 Indian Institutes of Management (IIM) and the Indian School of Business (ISB). ISB has a tie-up with Kellogg for its pedagogy.

clarifying_info.q: How do top schools in India select candidates?
clarifying_info.a: IIMs admit via the Common Admission Test (CAT). ISB admits candidates based on the GMAT.

clarifying_info.q: How expensive is an MBA education in India?
clarifying_info.a: It costs a student about $20,000 per year for an MBA education in India, compared to about $70,000 at Kellogg. Indian schools don't offer many scholarships but banks offer generous educational loans for top MBA schools in India.
Only the 2-year MBA program to start with.

exhibits.title: B-Schools in India
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of the two main competitor categories: Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) and Indian School of Business (ISB), covering admissions process details and cost incurred by students.

exhibits.title: Number of Admitted Students
exhibits.shows: A table showing the expected number of new students to be admitted at Kellogg India each year for Years 1 through 4.

data.note: Year 1 figure represents 7.5% of the total addressable market of 8,000

exhibits.title: Intake and Cost Structure
exhibits.shows: A table showing total variable costs per year for Years 1-4 and a breakdown of initial costs incurred in Year 0.

framework: Market Entry — Qualitative: assess brand impact/dilution, influence on rankings (diversity, international presence, % placements), cannibalization of existing Kellogg Indian students, brand parity with global employers, job prospects and ROI for students, infra and pedagogy support from parent campus

Market Entry — Quantitative: market sizing (total addressable market from IIM + ISB applicant pools), revenue model (fee per student per year x number of students x cohort accumulation), cost structure (initial/Year 0 costs + fixed + variable), breakeven analysis over 4 years
Revenue drivers: number of students admitted, fee charged per annum
Cost drivers: initial land/setup costs (Year 0), fixed annual costs (salaries, infrastructure maintenance), variable costs per student

questions.prompt: Estimate the Total Addressable Market (TAM) for Kellogg India.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use a bottom-up approach based on the high-quality applicant pools at IIMs and ISB. IIM: 500,000 applications → top 6% shortlisted = 30,000 → 1 in 5 accepted = 6,000 eligible students. ISB: 1,400 matriculated / 70% = 2,000 eligible students. TAM = 8,000 high-quality applicants. Then estimate market size: fee of ~$50,000/year (midpoint between $20k and $70k) for 2 years → $800M. A strong candidate notes 7.5% market share in Year 1 = 600 students.

math.answer: TAM = 8,000 high-quality applicants; Market size = $800M; Year 1 intake = 600 students

questions.prompt: Build the 4-year revenue and cost model and determine whether the campus breaks even within 4 years.
questions.guidance: Revenue: each cohort pays $50,000/year for 2 years, so revenue stacks as each year's cohort adds to prior year's second-year cohort. Costs: Year 0 initial = $150M; Years 1-4 variable costs from Exhibit C. A strong candidate asks for the discount rate; there is none given. The campus does NOT break even by Year 4 (cumulative profit = -$5M), but a top candidate notes it misses breakeven by only $5M and would break even in the first month of Year 5 given rising revenues and declining costs.

math.setup: Revenue each year = (new cohort × $50k) + (prior cohort × $50k if in year 2). Costs: Y0=$150M; Y1=$30M; Y2=$30M; Y3=$30M; Y4=$20M. Cumulative P&L from Y0 to Y4.
steps: Y2: 600 new + 600 returning = 1,200 students × $50k = $60M; cost = $30M; profit = $30M
Y3: 900 new + 600 returning = 1,500 students × $50k = $75M; cost = $30M; profit = $45M
Y4: 900 new + 900 returning = 1,800 students × $50k = $90M; cost = $20M; profit = $70M
Net after Y0 initial cost: $145M - $150M = -$5M (does not break even by Year 4)
Given Y4 monthly profit ≈ $70M/12 ≈ $5.8M/month, breakeven occurs in approximately the first month of Year 5
math.answer: Cumulative 4-year profit = $145M vs. $150M initial investment; misses breakeven by ~$5M. Breakeven achieved in approximately Month 1 of Year 5.

brainstorming.prompt: What qualitative factors should Kellogg consider before deciding to enter the Indian market?

categories.name: Brand Impact
ideas: No top US B-school (except INSEAD) has successfully started a satellite campus in India; risk of brand dilution must be assessed
Will global employers view an MBA from Kellogg India on par with Kellogg Evanston? Brand parity is unproven

categories.name: Rankings Impact
ideas: Satellite campus could positively impact diversity and international presence metrics
Job placement percentages and average salaries (calculated at Indian PPP) could drag down global ranking averages
Proximity to other Asian markets could attract regional talent and boost international diversity

categories.name: Cannibalization
ideas: Kellogg Evanston currently admits ~50-60 students per year from India; a local campus may divert these applications
Other Asian applicants may also redirect to Kellogg India, reducing quality pipeline to the main campus

categories.name: Job Prospects & ROI for Students
ideas: A significant premium over IIM/ISB is being charged ($50k vs. $20k/year); students must see commensurate salary uplift
ROI must be validated against Indian market salaries and global placement rates

categories.name: Infrastructure & Operations
ideas: Infra and pedagogy support from parent campus to satellite is critical
Faculty sourcing and quality parity need a concrete plan
Government approvals, land acquisition, and licensing in India are complex and time-consuming

categories.name: Financial Risks
ideas: Admission growth from Y2 to Y3 is projected at 50%; this is aggressive and may not materialize
$150M initial investment comes while Kellogg is also building a new building on its Evanston campus, requiring additional fundraising
Additional revenue sources (corporate training, executive education) should be explored to reduce breakeven risk

recommendation: From a quantitative standpoint, the satellite campus nearly breaks even in 4 years (misses by only $5M) and reaches breakeven in the first month of Year 5; the financial case is directionally sound
However, Kellogg should proceed cautiously: the brand impact and ranking implications of a satellite campus have not been validated and could outweigh the financial upside
risks: Brand dilution: no precedent of a top US B-school successfully running a satellite campus in India
Cannibalization of ~50-60 high-quality Indian students currently enrolling at Evanston
Salary reporting at Indian PPP levels may negatively impact Kellogg's global rankings
50% intake growth from Year 2 to Year 3 is aggressive and carries execution risk
$150M capital requirement conflicts with concurrent Evanston building investment
next_steps: Hire a brand agency to study the impact of a satellite campus on the Kellogg brand and rankings
Negotiate initial investment costs below $150M and explore Indian government subsidies
Develop additional revenue streams (corporate training, executive education) to accelerate breakeven
Identify potential academic partners (e.g., ISB, which already has a Kellogg pedagogy tie-up) to share faculty and infrastructure costs
Begin discussions with the Indian government on land, infrastructure investment, and licensing
